title: Ch3.6 · Nested queries and quantifiers
summary: Use IN, SOME, ALL, EXISTS, and NOT EXISTS to express membership, witnesses, and universal conditions.
objectives: Distinguish value membership from row existence
Translate SOME and ALL into witness reasoning
Use NOT EXISTS to express absence of a counterexample

sections.title: Nested queries and quantifiers
sections.body: A nested query is a relation-valued component of a larger query. First describe what the inner result means, then decide whether the outer condition needs membership, a witness, or the absence of a counterexample.

math.name: Universal condition
math.purpose: Use it when a request says every required item must be present.
math.explanation: Checking that no counterexample exists is often safer than relying on a nullable NOT IN subquery.

contrastDrills.pair: NOT IN vs NOT EXISTS with NULL
contrastDrills.prompt: A subquery can return {101, 102, NULL}. Which form is safer for finding students with no matching advisor row?
contrastDrills.explanation: A NULL in the `NOT IN` result can make the comparison UNKNOWN, so expected rows may disappear. A correlated `NOT EXISTS` directly checks that no matching advisor row exists.
contrastDrills.misconception: Assuming NOT IN remains a simple negation when its subquery contains NULL.
contrastDrills.repair: When NULL can enter the subquery, prefer a correlated NOT EXISTS or filter NULL explicitly before using NOT IN.
